title: Chorus Phasing Composer — timebox-driven cohort sequencing for canary & A/B
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and prototype a composable UI for sequencing phased exposures across temporal cohorts (timebox windows) supporting both canary and A/B experiments. The Composer should let operators author multi-step sequences with conditional gates, budget-aware traffic ramps, implicit rollback anchors, and instant preview of cost/latency impact per step.
background: Current Console rollout editors focus on single split/percentage edits and basic canaries. Teams frequently need to express time-windowed sequences (e.g., 10% for 4 hours, then 30% for 24 hours for cohort B, conditional hold or rollback) and estimate cost/latency implications for each phase. This effort explores a new composer paradigm that treats a rollout as an ordered choreography of cohorts with safety gates and cost signals.
goals: Provide a compact composer for sequencing phases with duration, traffic fraction, audiences, and conditional gates
Surface per-phase cost and expected P99 latency delta using historical model profiles
Make rollback anchors explicit and fast to trigger from composer or timeline
Support conversion between canary-style flows and A/B experiments without losing analytic continuity
Keep the entry flow lightweight for non-operator PMs while exposing advanced knobs for SREs
out_of_scope: Full experiment analytics and cohort creation UI (this design assumes cohorts are pre-defined via the Audience service). Deep integration with billing reconciliation is deferred to a follow-up.

acceptance_criteria: Hi-fi Figma prototype demonstrates: add/edit phase, set duration, traffic %, audience preset, and choose gate behavior
Composer displays per-phase cost estimate (tokens + infra) and expected latency delta using model profile approximation
Prototype includes a timeline preview mode that animates the sequence and highlights where rollbacks would occur
Design tokens and spacing follow Console theme; components are mapped to existing Console primitives for engineering handoff
Design notes list required server-side flags and API changes (phase KV pinning, scheduled phase activation, rollback API)
risks: Overloading the composer with too many knobs could increase cognitive load for non-SRE users
Cost estimates are approximations and could mislead operators if presented without confidence bounds
Requiring new server APIs (phase KV pinning) could delay delivery if not prioritized by platform team
decisions: Use a vertical, step-based composer (ordered phases) rather than an inline matrix to make conditional gates more visible
Expose a compact cost row per phase with hover for breakdown; do not show absolute forecasted billing at the top to avoid commitment
Provide two composer modes: Basic (percentage + duration) and Advanced (audience targeting, gate rules, cost knobs)
Rollback anchors are explicit per phase and trigger the existing emergency rollback flow in Console
